name: sol_defi_oracle_10
description: Oracle price update front-running enabling MEV extraction or unfair liquidation/trade execution
question: The source file in `source` contains a function that consumes or triggers an on-chain oracle price update and immediately allows a dependent state-changing action (such as a trade, mint/redeem, or liquidation) to execute using that same updated price within the same transaction or block, with no delay, commit-reveal step, or minimum-block-gap enforced between the price update and its use, allowing an attacker to front-run or back-run the update to profit; this excludes cases where prices are only read from an already-settled external feed without the contract itself triggering the update, or where a time delay, TWAP, or block-gap check already prevents same-block exploitation.
criteria: A function calls updatePrice() or similar on an oracle and then in the same call immediately executes a liquidation or trade using the freshly updated price with no delay check
A public function that anyone can call to push a new oracle price also permits, in the very next line or same transaction, minting/redeeming/borrowing at that new price
A liquidation function reads oracle.getLatestPrice() and liquidates immediately after a permissionless price push transaction with no minimum elapsed-block requirement
Swap or lending logic uses the spot price returned by an oracle update function without checking that at least N blocks have passed since the last price change
